references.text: Both texts deal with the duty to help a poor brother in need and give him what he requires.
The same chapter emphasizes that there will always be poor people in the land, and that one should open one's hand to them.
Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord, and He will reward their good deed.
Those who have a generous eye are blessed because they give of their bread to the poor.
The prophet Isaiah urges us to share our bread with the hungry and bring the homeless poor into our houses.
Ezekiel describes the righteous person as one who gives their bread to the hungry and clothes the naked.
Jesus teaches that we should give to those who ask, and not turn away from anyone who wants to borrow.
Jesus teaches about lending without expecting anything in return, and being merciful like the Father.
John asks how God's love can be in someone who has worldly wealth but shuts their heart against a brother in need.
